text:
marta: Quick heads-up — starting the Chronicle tenant_id type migration in the quiet window (03:00 UTC). I'm going to kick off the dry-run now, leaving the live rollout pinned until we confirm no lock storms.

deploy-bot: Migration dry-run initiated for `chronicle/tenantid-swap` at 2026-11-02T03:00:00Z. Tracking: RB-4871. Will post results when finished.

ashwin: thx. ping when dry-run finishes. if we see cross-tenant locks we should abort immediately.

kai: reminder: the dry-run needs to exercise the backfill path, not just DDL apply. last time we missed a KV cache hot path.

deploy-bot: Dry-run complete. Summary: DDL applied on canary DB, backfill executed on 4 partitions. Observed lock_wait spikes on partition range [tenant=42..48]. Max lock_wait 19.8s (20x baseline). See logs: https://logs.internal/chronicle/dryrun/1789997777

marta: ugh. that's higher than expected. Ashwin, can you grep for concurrent writers around tenant 42?

ashwin: checking. quick output: `SELECT count(*) FROM jobs WHERE tenant_id BETWEEN 42 AND 48 AND state = 'running';` -> 17 (normally 1-2). Looks like scheduled nightly jobs overlapped the dry-run window.

kai: if it's job overlap, we can (1) pause those jobs for the live window, (2) run targeted backfill on replicas, or (3) do tenant-level staged switchover. which is least risky?

release-coordinator: Options ranked: 1) Pause jobs + retry live rollout (low infra change). 2) Staged switchover per-tenant with deploybot routing (more manual ops). 3) Cancel and reschedule to a quieter window (fallback). Decision needs owner & ETA.

marta: prefer 1 first. can we gate job runner for tenants in the quiet window? SRE?

sre-bot: Runbook snippet: 
```
-- Pause job runner for tenant range 42-48
UPDATE scheduled_jobs SET enabled = false WHERE tenant_id BETWEEN 42 AND 48;
-- Verify no running jobs
SELECT id FROM jobs WHERE tenant_id BETWEEN 42 AND 48 AND state = 'running';
```

ashwin: I can flip enabled=false in 5m, but need a safety escape hatch: if backfill still contends, we'll revert and pin the migration (no live traffic).

marta: agreed. deploy-bot, pin the live rollout while we coordinate the pause.

deploy-bot: Command accepted: `pin-rollout chronicle/tenantid-swap --version=2026.11.3 --reason="pause for targeted job freeze"` — rollout pinned.

kai: after we pause jobs, let's run a targeted backfill on replica set `chr-replica-7` with throttling and KV cache warmup. command:
```
./backfill --tenant-range=42-48 --replica=chr-replica-7 --rate=1000/s --kv-warmup=true
```

ashwin: starting pause now. will monitor job queue.

sre-bot: Alert: scheduled_jobs rows updated for tenant 42-48. Verification: 0 running jobs found.

ashwin: kicked off backfill to replica with `--rate=500/s` (safer). initial tail: "progress 1.2% — 3 partitions completed"

marta: nice. keep an eye on lock_wait. if <2s across the range for 5m, we can unpin and start live rollout in canary mode.

deploy-bot: Backfill task created: BF-9923 on chr-replica-7. ETA ~45m at current rate.

kai: small note: ensure we don't run the full parallel reindex on primary during this window. set `maintenance.mode=reduced` for deploy agent.

release-coordinator: Acked. I toggled maintenance flag in the console.

sre-bot: Monitoring: lock_wait 95th percentile across tenant 42-48 dropped from 19.8s -> 1.3s after pause.

marta: good signal. ashwin, once backfill finishes, can you run a quick canary apply for tenant 42 only? one-host canary.

ashwin: scheduled canary apply for tenant 42 at 03:55 UTC. Will use `apply-mode=canary-host`.

deploy-bot: Canary apply initiated for tenant 42. Will report result.

ashwin: canary finished — apply succeeded, no elevated lock waits, tests passed.

marta: sweet. ready to unpin and proceed? we should do a staged rollout: tenants 42-44, then 45-48, watching metrics between waves.

kai: +1. wave size: 3 tenants per wave, 10m observability window. rollback hatch: `deploybot abort-rollout --tag=chronicle/tenantid-swap`

marta: deploy-bot, unpin and start staggered rollout per plan.

deploy-bot: Unpin accepted. Beginning staged rollout: wave 1 tenants 42-44 -> wave 2 tenants 45-48. Wave gap: 10m. Notifying oncall.

sre-bot: Oncall notified: @oncall-db. Lock wait stayed stable during wave 1.

release-coordinator: Wave 1 ✅. Wave 2 started. Reminder: if any single tenant exceeds 5s p95 lock_wait, trigger immediate rollback and re-pin.

marta: wave 2 observed a transient 6.2s p95 on tenant 46 after a background analytics job sneaked in — I scaled the analytics job down for that tenant. Lock waits returned to 1.8s. continuing.

ashwin: rollout complete for all tenants in range. Post-migration checklist: run `data-compat-check --range=42-48` and `kv-cache-prime` for affected services.

marta: running checks now.

deploy-bot: Rollout complete. Closing RB-4871. Release note draft posted to #release-notes: "Chronicle tenant_id type migration applied for tenants 42-48 with staged rollout; no customer-facing downtime."

release-coordinator: Drafted release note: will add perf numbers and link to runbook before pushing external note.

marta: huge thanks to everyone — especially Ashwin for fast job freezes and Kai for throttled backfill. :tada:

ashwin: nice teamwork. can we add a small automation to detect and pause scheduled_jobs automatically for tenant-range migrations?

kai: +1. follow-up ticket: AUTO-2445 — auto-pause scheduled_jobs + preflight check.

deploy-bot: Ticket AUTO-2445 created and linked to RB-4871.

release-coordinator: closing thread, moving notes to the migration postmortem doc.

marta: closing — will add runbook snippet with the exact SQL + deploybot commands used.
